cands.name: Brent Andersen
cands.bio: Republican nominee. Pompano Beach insurance broker and businessman who moved to Florida in 2021; wife is Venezuelan. Has not held office. Won a four-way GOP primary. District 20 now lies entirely in central Broward County and is heavily Democratic.
cands.local_ties: Pompano Beach; in Florida since 2021, close to family.

record.text: Platform (Diario Las Americas interview): cut waste and fraud in federal programs, faster legal immigration, fewer housing regulations, more domestic energy, federal action on insurance costs, no Social Security/Medicare cuts, Second Amendment with limits aimed at criminals, strongly pro-life.
Challenged Wasserman Schultz to three debates (Florida's Voice headline; page not opened).

endorsements.text: Sun Sentinel editorial board (also endorsed Wasserman Schultz in the same race), Log Cabin Republicans, state Rep. Chip LaMarca (as listed on Wikipedia).

cands.gaps: No photo, working campaign site or verified social accounts found (brentandersen.com is a parked page). No fundraising or outside-spending detail. Some outlets spell his name 'Anderson'.

cands.name: Debbie Wasserman Schultz
cands.bio: Democrat, U.S. House since 2005 (previously FL-25). Florida House 1992-2000 and Florida Senate 2000-2004. DNC chair 2011-2016. Sits on Appropriations (ranking member, Military Construction-VA subcommittee). In the Aug 2026 primary she beat four Black challengers, 45.6%, after the new map reshaped her seat.
cands.local_ties: Long-time Broward resident; moved into the new District 20 (central and western Broward, majority-Black communities) after the 2026 map; critics said a Black candidate should hold the seat, she cited experience and winning top Black-majority precincts.

record.text: Chair of the House Democratic Steering Committee since 2023; Appropriations subcommittees on Agriculture/FDA, Energy and Water, and Military Construction-VA (ranking member).
Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary: Wasserman Schultz 45.6% (29,759), Dale Holness 22.9%, Elijah Manley 13.9%, Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick 9.2%, Luther Campbell 8.4% (99% counted).
After the primary she said voters care most about affordability and rejected 'fringe left socialism'; Hakeem Jeffries declined to endorse her bid in this district (Jewish Insider, June 2026).

money_notes.text: AIPAC, Democratic Majority for Israel, Jewish Democratic Council of America, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Giffords, LCV, Florida AFL-CIO and Broward Teachers Union endorsed her in the primary (Wikipedia list); progressive challenger Elijah Manley campaigned against her AIPAC ties (JTA/JPost coverage). No super PAC spending totals for this race were found.

controversies.text: Resigned as DNC chair July 28, 2016 after WikiLeaks published DNC emails showing staff favoring Hillary Clinton over Bernie Sanders in the primary.

2017 Capitol Police accusations against House IT staffers (the Awan brothers) who worked for her and other members; Imran Awan pleaded guilty in 2018 to a bank-loan false statement, and prosecutors said they found no evidence of illegal conduct involving House computer systems.
2026: Broward Black Democrats and top state Democrats criticized her decision to run in the historically Black District 20 rather than a different seat.

endorsements.text: Miami Herald and Sun Sentinel editorial boards; Broward Teachers Union; Florida AFL-CIO; National Education Association (post-primary); Equality PAC (shared with Manley in primary) per Wikipedia.
